title: Edge Cases Break The System
summary: This failure describes systems that do not maintain coherent behaviour when edge case conditions occur. It covers undefined behaviour, invalid state combinations, cascading failures, faulty error handling, and sensor or data edge cases in embedded systems.
keyFacts: Every system is designed for a set of conditions; this failure occurs when conditions outside that designed set produce behaviour that was never designed.
The failure is about system breakage, not merely poor interaction support for rare scenarios.
Invalid state combinations can be individually valid at component level but collectively undefined at system level.
Cascading failures can occur when one component's edge case triggers unexpected behaviour in other components.
Error handling can worsen the failure when recovery states, timeouts, or validation rules create more damaging states than the original condition.
Embedded systems can encounter sensor edge cases such as dropouts, conflicting readings, delayed readings, or out-of-range values that are physically possible but outside interface assumptions.
Gexcon CFD simulation work involved contradictory parameter combinations that were individually valid but collectively inconsistent.
Cox Marine cluster display scenario testing included a multi-engine fault scenario during Concept Convergence.
KISPE Space produced 40 documented edge cases and degraded states with 12 annotated plates as specifications, not executed tests.
The KISPE Space catalogue was specified against a synthetic demonstration fixture and was never exercised against a running system.

bodySections.heading: What Edge Case Breakage Means in Complex Software
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

Edge case breakage is a failure mode in which inputs or conditions outside the designed normal case push a system into undefined behaviour, invalid states, misleading outputs, or non-functional lock-in. The interface may enter an incoherent state, generate an output with no valid operational interpretation, or prevent the user from continuing.

This failure is not the same as weak support for unusual scenarios. Poor support means the system still has a valid state but does not help the user enough. Edge case breakage means the system has no coherent designed behaviour for the condition it has entered.

bodySections.heading: Undefined Behaviour Under Edge Case Conditions
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Edge case breakage appears when a system encounters a condition outside its designed envelope and falls back on default state machinery rather than designed behaviour. The resulting state may be technically representable by the software but operationally invalid.

Undefined behaviour is the central risk. The system may continue running while presenting information that looks coherent, even though the underlying state has no valid interpretation. In other cases, the system becomes non-functional because it cannot proceed and cannot return to a known safe state.

An edge case is not necessarily rare. It is an input or condition outside the designed normal case. A condition can be foreseeable and still break the system if no behaviour was designed for it.

bodySections.heading: How Edge Cases Create Invalid System States
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Edge cases break systems when the interface has no designed response outside the normal operating case. When edge cases are treated as out of scope or deferred for later design, the system may fall back on behaviour produced by its implementation rather than behaviour specified for the user and the operation.

Invalid state combinations are a common mechanism. In complex systems with interdependent parameters, separate components can each hold values that are individually valid while the combined state is undefined. The system then behaves unpredictably because the combined state was never designed.

Cascading failures occur when an edge case in one component triggers unexpected behaviour in other components. The original edge case may be manageable, but the downstream state becomes unmanageable because other parts of the system were not designed to handle upstream abnormality.

Error handling can also create edge case breakage. An error handler can move the system into the wrong recovery state, a timeout can lock an incomplete configuration, or a validation rule can reject a valid edge case input without explanation. In these cases, the response to the edge case produces a worse state than the original condition.

Embedded systems add sensor and data edge cases. Sensor dropouts, conflicting sensor readings, delayed readings, and out-of-range values can be technically possible while still sitting outside the interface's data assumptions. The display may then show stale values, contradictory values, or values that conflate a fault with a real state change.

bodySections.heading: Designed Responses Keep Edge Cases Out of Undefined Behaviour
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Defensive design is the alternative to assuming edge cases will not occur. The system needs specified behaviour for inputs outside the normal case, including what is displayed, what is blocked, what is degraded, and what recovery path is available.

Graceful degradation is one designed response to edge case pressure. Instead of entering an undefined state, the system continues with reduced capability and makes the degraded condition visible. This preserves a valid operational state even when full normal operation is not possible.

Designed edge case handling can include contradictory-input detection before a run begins, visible fault states for sensors, delayed-reading states, restart points after hardware communication failure, and aggregate fault summaries that prevent multiple valid component states from becoming an incoherent display state.

bodySections.heading: Boundaries With Adjacent Failure Modes
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Edge case breakage differs from poor interaction support for rare scenarios. Rare-scenario support can be weak while the system still remains in a valid state. Edge case breakage means the system enters an undefined, incoherent, misleading, or non-functional state.

Edge case breakage also differs from weak recovery paths. Weak recovery paths concern what happens after an error has already been identified. Edge case breakage concerns the system's failure to maintain coherent state when an edge case condition is encountered, before recovery is attempted.

The evidence base for this failure includes different evidential classes. Field-observed or scenario-tested design findings should not be blended with specification evidence. Specification evidence supports the value of defining edge case behaviour in advance; it does not support claims about executed validation unless that validation is separately evidenced.

strongClaims: Edge case breakage occurs when inputs or conditions outside the designed normal case produce undefined, incoherent, misleading, or non-functional system behaviour.
Invalid state combinations can occur when components are individually valid but collectively undefined.
Cascading failures can occur when an edge case in one component triggers unexpected behaviour in other components.
Error handling can worsen edge case breakage when recovery states, timeouts, or validation rules produce states worse than the original condition.
The Gexcon CFD simulation work used contradictory-input detection to prevent collectively contradictory parameter combinations from producing coherent-looking outputs from incoherent inputs.
The Cox Marine cluster display work used a simulated multi-engine fault scenario during Concept Convergence and added a dedicated fault-summary area with per-tile alarm highlighting.
The Beissbarth automotive calibration work specified display behaviour, technician action, and restart point for equipment communication failure.
The KISPE Space work produced 40 documented edge cases and degraded states with 12 annotated plates as specifications, not executed tests.
The KISPE Space catalogue was specified against a synthetic demonstration fixture and was never exercised against a running system.
limitations: This page distinguishes edge case breakage from poor interaction support for rare scenarios; it does not treat all rare-scenario problems as system breakage.
This page distinguishes edge case breakage from weak recovery paths; recovery path weakness begins after an error has been identified.
The case examples are evidentially different: running-system and scenario-tested examples must not be blended with KISPE Space specification evidence.
KISPE Space's 40 edge cases, verification checks, and recovery paths are specifications, not completed testing.
The KISPE Space catalogue was not validated with users or on hardware in the described evidence.
The KISPE Space product was built, but Creative Navy did not support the build and has not compared the built interface against the delivered designs.
